- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is below recent low, model tends to undercorrect — adjust upward slightly to avoid missing upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots — cap forecast peak at 1.5–2x prior high or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is positive and forecast is consistently below true outcome, model underestimates bullish momentum — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day if sentiment > 0.2.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show forecast > true, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per day to avoid overbought overcorrection.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price rise — add 0.5–1.0% buffer to final 10 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly negative and forecast is flat, model tends to lag — add 0.2–0.5% upward bias to catch momentum.
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 18-day low unless sentiment is strongly negative — model often underestimates downside risk in bearish sentiment.
